identification.discovery: Electrolux/Frigidaire app and cloud account enumeration

device.name: Frigidaire WiFi Window Air Conditioner
device.notes:
WiFi-connected window AC units controlled via the Frigidaire app (Electrolux platform). Covers FHWW series (8K-24K BTU; the range extends to the 24,000 BTU FHWW245WE2) and Gallery GHWQ series. Cloud-connected via Electrolux OCP servers. The ionizer (Clean Air) feature is model-specific, not Gallery-wide: the official GHWQ083WC1 spec sheet states "Clean Air Ionizer: No", while older Gallery Cool Connect models (e.g. FGRC104WA1) do have one.
DISCOVERY/AUTHENTICATION: this is WiFi cloud control, not a steady-state local LAN protocol. APK static analysis of Frigidaire com.electrolux.oneapp.android.frigidaire v1.24, v2.0, and v3.6 found OCP cloud endpoints and websocket hosts, plus provisioning-only local paths: SoftAP SSID hints (AJ, @E, IOT, Air_Conditioner, Dehumidifier), Delta NIU TCP/TLS setup, AllJoyn onboarding/enrollment classes, UDP broadcast on port 3000, a direct setup connection to 192.168.6.1:3002, and in v2.0 a cleartext network-security exception for 192.168.0.1. Searches for mDNS/NSD, SSDP/UPnP, .local service discovery, local REST/websocket endpoints, LAN control feature flags, and AWS Greengrass/local proxy patterns found no usable post-pairing LAN discovery/control path for these AC units.
Discovery for users happens through the Frigidaire/Electrolux app account after app-based pairing. The replacement control path must authenticate to the Electrolux cloud/OCP account, enumerate appliances assigned to that account, then send commands through the cloud API or websocket. An official path now exists alongside the reverse-engineered OCP one: the Electrolux Developer API (developer.electrolux.one) plus the official Apache-2.0 Python SDK (electrolux-oss/electrolux-group-developer-sdk), reported to work with NA-region Frigidaire 2.0 app credentials.
Protocol details still need network captures to confirm exact request and payload formats, but local device discovery is closed as cloud-only for post-pairing control based on the inspected APK.

factory_reset.effect: Clears WiFi credentials and the account binding, returning the unit to pairing mode. Vendor-documented in an official Frigidaire support article (the router-change procedure).

steps.action: Remove the appliance from the Frigidaire 2.0 app.
Press and hold the Wi-Fi/Connect button for 10 seconds (the unit may beep).
Unplug the appliance for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
steps.notes: Wait at least 60 seconds after plugging back in before attempting the connection process again.

cloud.local_alternative: None found. The local API audit across firmware v1.24, v2.0 and v3.6 confirmed there is no local HTTP, SSDP or mDNS control surface to fall back on.

methods.description: The vendor app puts the appliance into pairing mode, transfers the home network credentials, and registers the appliance against an Electrolux account. Neither the credential transfer nor the registration handshake has been captured here.

steps.action: Put the unit into pairing mode from its own control panel.
steps.notes: Typically holding the WiFi/Connect button until the WiFi indicator blinks; confirm against the model's manual.

steps.action: Complete onboarding in the vendor app, which transfers credentials and registers the appliance.

steps.notes: Open gap: the highest-value capture target for this device, since it is the only moment local credentials are in play.

setup.notes: Onboarding is cloud-mediated and is the reason this appliance has no local control story: the unit is bound to an Electrolux account during setup, and every documented control path goes back through that account. See the local API audit for the evidence that no local endpoint survives provisioning.

rejoin.notes: Changing routers means re-running app onboarding. If the vendor cloud is retired, that path disappears and the unit cannot be re-bound at all — the practical definition of a bricked smart appliance. This is not hypothetical for this device family: Frigidaire deactivated the 1.0 Smart App outright and required owners to re-onboard their appliances to the Frigidaire 2.0 app.

entities.name: Air Conditioner
entities.notes: OCP wire names below come from the app's bundled capability profile (ac_daiane_capabilities.json) and its attribute-name enum; medium confidence, app-derived, not verified against hardware. targetTemperatureC is readwrite, 16-30 C in steps of 1 (the app's attribute enum also maps a targetTemperatureF attribute; the bundled profiles declare only the C spelling). hvac_mode values are AUTO/COOL/FANONLY/HEAT; eco is not a mode value but the separate energySavingMode attribute. fan_mode values are AUTO/HIGH/MIDDLE/LOW/TURBO (the profile's spelling is "MIDDLE", not Medium). Power is the write-only executeCommand attribute with values ON/OFF. Every `commands` value in this and the other entities below is an OCP attribute write sent to the "Appliance Command" endpoint (PUT .../appliances/{applianceId}/command); see that endpoint's description for the encoding — a bare attribute name writes the control's value to that attribute, and "attribute=VALUE" writes the literal VALUE.

entities.name: Room Temperature
entities.notes: ambientTemperatureC is the wire name in the app's attribute enum, but the bundled daiane profile declares no ambient-temperature attribute; low confidence until a traffic capture confirms it.

entities.name: Filter Alert
entities.notes: filterState is a read-only enum (GOOD/CLEAN/CHANGE/BUY); any value other than GOOD is a problem state. cleanFilterAlertReset is a write-only attribute that clears the alert.

entities.name: Sleep Mode
entities.notes: sleepMode attribute (readwrite, OFF/ON) per the app's attribute enum and the bundled emmanuelle capability profiles; the daiane window-AC profile omits it, so availability on window units is unverified. Medium confidence.

entities.name: Display
entities.notes: displayLight is an enum (DISPLAY_LIGHT_0/DISPLAY_LIGHT_100), not a boolean; the daiane profile declares it readwrite.

entities.name: Energy Saving (Eco)
entities.notes: energySavingMode attribute (readwrite, OFF/ON) — eco is this separate attribute, not a value of mode. Per the daiane profile's triggers, turning it ON removes TURBO from the allowed fanSpeedSetting values.

entities.name: Clean Air (Ionizer)
entities.notes: cleanAirMode attribute (OFF/ON). The daiane profile marks it access 'read', so write support is unverified and the commands below are low confidence.

http_endpoints.description: Cloud command path; path and PUT method confirmed in the app's endpoint enum (PUT_SEND_COMMAND). Payload is a single-property JSON map keyed by an OCP attribute name, e.g. {"fanSpeedSetting": "LOW"} or {"executeCommand": "ON"}, sent one property per call (medium confidence, app-derived, not hardware-verified; exact serialization requires traffic capture). This endpoint is the encoding referenced by every entity `commands` value in this spec. Those values use two forms: a bare OCP attribute name (e.g. set_temperature -> "targetTemperatureC") means "PUT this attribute with the value the control supplies", i.e. {"<attribute>": <control value>}; the form "<attribute>=<VALUE>" (e.g. turn_on -> "executeCommand=ON") means "PUT this attribute with the literal VALUE", i.e. {"<attribute>": "<VALUE>"}. There are no separately declared command blocks because OCP control is attribute writes, not named commands.
